The investigation traced 14 distinct blockchain entities linked to the seed wallet 0xa7f39c1d8e4b2a5f7c3d9e0a1b8c6d4e5f2a67e9, involving 17 transfers across a maximum depth of three hops. Sixteen transfers are confirmed, with one inferred correlation, and 16 of the transfers meet or exceed the 30 % reporting threshold. The fund movement shows rapid automated dispersal, with the first outbound transaction occurring three minutes after receipt, followed by interaction with a mixer contract (address 0x8589f2c47b1d0a63e95482f7ca1b3d6e0f4a0b6f) handling 1,500 USDT, and subsequent exposure to a cross‑chain bridge (address 0xbb17d4a09e26c35f81b0d7a94e13c68f05b2c530) within two downstream hops.

Risk scoring assigns a high rating of 65/100 to the seed wallet, reflecting proximity to a known scam cluster (+20), rapid automated dispersal (+15), mixer interaction (+15) and bridge exposure (+15). The highest‑scoring entity observed is address 0x9c04a7e3b21d5f86c0a94e7d2b83f150c6ead21e with a critical score of 75/100; the seed wallet remains at a high score of 65/100, while address 0x3f1a7d92c04e8b56af10d3e7b829c45d6e0a71bc scores 35/100 (medium).
